text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to discuss in Cairo today latest developments of the peace process.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri starts a tour of Malaysia, Singapore and China at the beginning of Egyptian moves at international and Arab levels to help economic development. Ganzouri arrives in Kuala Lumpur yesterday evening. Before leaving Cairo, Ganzouri says the Egyptian economy is ready to receive large capital inflows.
- Investors can start their projects without prior official approval. Public Enterprise Minister, Atef Obeid, says new decisions will be issued in the next few days to encourgae investement in Egypt.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says that Egypt is studying sending a delegation to America to discuss the issue of settlement in the occupied lands. Moussa tells reporters that any unbalanced initiative will not succeed.
- Moustafa Amin, pioneer of contemporary Arab journalism, died at the age of 83.
- Cabinet will discuss the draft budget after the holiday of Eid al-Adha. The budget, which totals 84 billion pounds ($24.7 billion), includes 23.4 billion pounds for salaries and subsidy.

- Mubarak says he will send an Egyptian envoy to America tomorrow, after receiving a letter from U.S. President Bill Clinton. In an exclusive interview with Chief Editor Samir Ragab, Mubarak says that his political adviser Usama el-Baz will fly to Washington. "President Clinton confirmed in this message his and the U.S. appreciation to the Egyptian role in pushing the peace process forward," Mubarak adds.
